title: Symbiotic Co-evolutionary Dynamics and Simulation of the Agricultural Production Trusteeship Service Ecosystem
content: To unveil the "black box" of internal evolution within agricultural production trusteeship services, this study constructs a symbiotic co-evolution model of the service ecosystem based on symbiosis theory and complex adaptive systems theory, incorporating trusteeship organizations and smallholders as core agents. By analyzing equilibrium points and stability conditions of the dual-agent dynamic model, numerical simulations reveal symbiotic patterns between these agents. To overcome limitations of dyadic evolution, the government is introduced as a third agent, extending the model to a tripartite framework. Further simulations examine how government intervention influences symbiotic relationships and evolutionary trajectories. Key findings include:(1) The agricultural production trusteeship service ecosystem constitutes a coordinated system formed by three symbiotic units-trusteeship smallholders, trusteeship organizations, and the government-through diverse symbiotic interactions to deliver trusteeship services. (2) The system and its three agents undergo synchronized co-evolution, with stability contingent upon symbiotic coefficients among agents and their respective growth efficiency ceilings. When all coefficients are positive, the maximum growth potential of each agent is enhanced.(3) Symbiotic evolution is inherently dynamic: system trajectories and stability conditions diverge across symbiotic modes, with relationships transitioning from parasitic and commensalistic to ultimately mutualistic symbiosis.(4) Government involvement significantly elevates system stability and sustainability, shatters growth ceilings inherent in dyadic systems, and steers the ecosystem toward tripartite mutualism. Finally, optimization strategies are proposed across three dimensions: coordinating symbiotic units、strengthening symbiotic interfaces、optimizing symbiotic environments.
